model_annotation: Figure 2 presents an accuracy matrix illustrating the performance of several machine learning models trained on different combinations of data sets, categorized by specialty area. The horizontal axis, labeled “Test Sets” and ranging from (80) to (102), displays the different test sets used in the experiment, ordered alphabetically from “Cardio” to “Rodiatrics.” The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, extends from 33.7 to 49.1 and uses a linear scale, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 4 or 5 percentage points. There are six bar groups, each representing a unique combination of data sets: “Cardio,” “Gastro,” “Infect,” “Neuro,” “Obstetrics,” and “Rodiatrics.” The “Cardio” bar group contains bars colored in shades of blue, with the tallest bar representing a value of 51.8% and the shortest bar representing 44.3%. The “Gastro” bar group consists of bars colored in shades of green, with a maximum value of 45.9% and a minimum value of 43.9%. The “Infect” bar group is represented by bars colored in shades of red, with a maximum of 54.9% and a minimum of 43.5%. The “Neuro” bar group displays bars of yellow, with the highest value of 58.4% and the lowest of 41.9%. The “Obstetrics” bar group features bars colored in shades of pink, with a maximum value of 54.4% and a minimum value of 43.4%. Finally, the “Rodiatrics” bar group consists of bars colored in shades of orange, with a maximum value of 49.1% and a minimum of 33.7%. All bars are presented without any visual emphasis, and the bars are not sorted in a specific order.
